facts.content: Patient reports wheeze and shortness of breath for 2 to 3 days.
facts.source_text: CC: Wheeze and SOB x 2–3 d

facts.content: Patient has a dry cough and felt feverish with a temperature of 37°C.
facts.source_text: HPI: Cough (dry), felt fever; measured T 37°C.

facts.content: Patient experiences dyspnea on exertion and sometimes has difficulty finishing sentences.
facts.source_text: DOE; sometimes hard to finish sentences.

facts.content: Shortness of breath occurs on walking but not at rest, does not wake patient at night.
facts.source_text: SOB on walking, none at rest. Not waking at night.

facts.content: Patient is unable to walk to work but currently feels well and is able to climb stairs.
facts.source_text: Unable to walk to work; currently feels well; able to climb stairs.

facts.content: Patient had childhood asthma which was severe enough to require hospital visits but not ICU admission.
facts.source_text: PMH: Childhood asthma (quite bad; hospital visits, no ICU)

facts.content: Patient has a history of hay fever.
facts.source_text: PMH: hay fever

facts.content: Patient has a history of eczema.
facts.source_text: PMH: eczema

facts.content: Patient uses a Salbutamol inhaler as needed, every few weeks or before exercise.
facts.source_text: Meds: Salbutamol inhaler PRN (every few wks; before exercise sometimes).

facts.content: Patient is not on any other medications.
facts.source_text: No other meds.

facts.content: Patient has no known drug allergies.
facts.source_text: Allergies: NKDA

facts.content: Patient has never smoked and drinks about one glass of wine every 2 to 3 days.
facts.source_text: Never smoker. etOH ~1 glass wine q2–3 d.

facts.content: Patient lives with a partner and works as an engineer.
facts.source_text: Lives w/ partner. Engineer.

facts.content: Patient is working from home or on sick leave due to symptoms.
facts.source_text: WFH/sick leave due to sx.

facts.content: Asthma exacerbation for 2 to 3 days with wheeze, dyspnea on exertion, and dry cough, possibly triggered by allergies or a virus.
facts.source_text: Asthma exacerbation x 2–3 d: wheeze, DOE, dry cough; afebrile; no rest dyspnea; intermittent speech limitation. Possible allergic or viral trigger.

facts.content: Patient has allergic rhinitis.
facts.source_text: Allergic rhinitis (hay fever)

facts.content: Increase use of Salbutamol to 2–4 puffs every 4 hours initially for asthma exacerbation.
facts.source_text: Increase SABA: salbutamol 2–4 puffs q4h initially

facts.content: Prescribe a spacer and have the pharmacist teach its use.
facts.source_text: Prescribe spacer; pharmacist to teach use

facts.content: Prescribe a peak flow meter and record peak expiratory flow morning and evening for one week.
facts.source_text: Prescribe peak flow meter; record PEF AM and PM x 1 wk

facts.content: Give safety-net advice to call back urgently if fever develops or wheeze/shortness of breath worsens.
facts.source_text: Safety-net: call back urgently if fever develops or wheeze/SOB worsens

facts.content: Arrange asthma review in approximately one week and consider controller inhaler based on PEF and symptoms.
facts.source_text: Arrange asthma review in ~1 wk (earlier if worse); consider controller inhaler pending PEF/sx

facts.content: Start regular over-the-counter antihistamine for allergic rhinitis with pharmacist advice on choice.
facts.source_text: Start regular OTC antihistamine; pharmacist advice on choice
